title: JD Vance contradicts Trump with ‘give us another chance’ flub | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

Vice President JD Vance this week asked voters for “another chance” — something that is decidedly contrary to President Donald Trump’s midterm messaging — before seeming to catch himself.

“Give us another chance — or, give us another couple of years to continue to work on the amazing things that we’ve been doing for the past two years,” Vancesaid on the “All In” podcast.

A couple of reflections.

The first is that Vance seemed to think better of the phrase he had just uttered and tried to change it. Indeed, asking for “another chance” sure makes it sound like Republicans haven’t succeeded with the chance they’ve been given.

His comment is also decidedly different from what Trump says, which is all about the “golden age” and how everything is so great in the United States.

Vance has been offering a more nuanced and conciliatory message to voters who might be disillusioned, ashis speech last weekat the Republican midterm convention made abundantly clear. In that speech, in his “All In” appearance and inclosed-door remarks to House Republicansthis week, Vance made a point to acknowledge the concerns of voters who might not like everything the administration has done, like the Iran war, or are struggling financially.

“Right now, we have a country where people are frustrated. You got to level with them,” he advised GOP lawmakers, according to a recording of the meeting obtained by CNN.

But there’s a difference between “I feel your pain” or acknowledging discontent, and “give us another chance.”

This is also the latest evidence that Vance, despite being the odds-on favorite for the Republican presidential nomination in 2028, just isn’t that gifted a messenger. Everyone assumes he’s the heir to Trump’s political movement, but he’s not a natural on the stump, by any means, and his ability to lock down the Trumpian base is very much to be determined.

But perhaps the biggest point is that whichever version of this talking point Vance offers — be it “another chance” or “another couple of years” — it’s virtually irreconcilable with the campaign that Trump ran in 2024.

The message back then wasn’t just that Trump would fix the problems created by then-President Joe Biden; it was that he would do so thoroughly and quickly.

Iran through some of the promisesa week before Trump took office:

The 2024 campaign was hardly the only time Trump promised voters the world. This is a guy who in 2016 literally said, “I will give you everything.”

But the broken promises are much more difficult to ignore when the consequences are so roundly despised by voters. Maybe Trump didn’t make everyone rich like he promised in 2016, but the economy was still pretty strong before Covid. Today, his promise to lower prices instantly looks worse with each passing day, and three-quarters of Americansthink he’s neglected the issue.

Ditto the Iran war. It’s so contrary to how Trump pitched himself, and it won’t go away.

And that’s what makes Vance’s comments particularly jarring.

Even more than his somewhat conciliatory speech last week at the GOP midterm convention, they suggest he knows the Trump administration hasn’t delivered on what it promised.

Before he said “another chance,” he listed a number of administration accomplishments. But none of them were about lowering prices across the board or delivering a new “golden age” for the American people. They were narrower items like “no tax on tips” and securing the border.

And that’s a pretty remarkable lack of an endorsement, from Trump’s own VP.
